To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the striosomes and extratriosomal matrix of the mature striatum are characterized by differences in TyrOHase-like immunoactivity.

the distribution of fibers expressing tyrosine hydroxy-like immunoreactivity is distinctively inhomogeneous in the mature striata of human, monkey, cat, and rat brains and that the macroscopic compartments called striosomes have relatively low tyrosine hydroxlase-like immunoreactive fiber density relative to the extrastriosomal striatum.
the mesostriate innervation of striosomal compartments is less rich in TyrOHase-like immuoreactivity than the innervation of the extrastriosomal compartments in mature human and monkey brains.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of immunohistochemical methods that permit the identification of neurons containing tyrosine hydroxylation activity and the localization of the enzyme in their axons and terminals.
the development and application of immunocytochemical methods to study the organization of the dopaminergie mesostriatal system.
the organization of the mesostriatum in the human, monkey, cat, rat, and mouse brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mesostriatonigral dopaminergic innervation is organized into a mosaic-like distribution of fibers in the striatal matrix and that the striosomal compartment is relatively devoid of such fibers.
the striatum is not a homogeneous structure, and that the distribution of dopaminergic innervation is inhomogeneous, with the highest density in the matrix and the lowest in the striosomes.

the distribution of TyrOHase-like-immunoreactive fibers in the mature striatal compartment is heterogeneous, with the extrastriosomal striatal matrix containing a higher concentration of TyrOHase than the striosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
striosomes are a unique compartment in the mature striatal circuitry that may serve as a locus of differential modulation by dopamine.
the mesostriatonigral and mesolimbic pathways of the mature primate brain are characterized by a mosaic pattern of TyrOHase-like-immunoreactive fibers.
TyrOHase-like expression in the striatum is not uniform and may vary in a way that reflects a fundamental difference in the function of the two compartments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
striosomes and extratiosomal matrix are different.
striosomes are not just a structural feature of the striatum.
the distribution of TyrOHase in striosomes and extratiosomal matrix is not uniform, but instead, the extrastriosomal compartment is more densely innervated than the striosome compartment.
